sample_unit: images read in multireader multicase study by 28 otolaryngologists

links.outcome: Otolaryngologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in multireader multicase study
links.effect: Primary care otolaryngologists' accuracy rose 7.9%, from 83.4% (95% CI 80.1-86.7) without AI to 91.2% (88.6-93.9) with AI (p<0.0001); reading time fell from 6.7 s to 5.0 s.
links.quote: In the multireader, multicase study, the artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategy enhanced otolaryngologists' diagnostic accuracy by 7·9%, increasing from 83·4% (95% CI 80·1-86·7, without AI assistance) to 91·2% (95% CI 88·6-93·9, with AI assistance; p<0·0001) for primary care otolaryngologists.

links.outcome: Model performance on prospectively acquired external multisite validation images versus internal dataset
links.effect: Internal AUC 0.99 for NPC vs non-malignant; external validation on 1885 prospective images from ten hospitals gave AUC 0.95, sensitivity 91.6%, specificity 86.1%.
links.quote: In the external validation, the system had an AUC for the detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma of 0·95 (95% CI 0·94-0·96), a sensitivity of 91·6% (95% CI 89·3-93·5), and a specificity of 86·1% (95% CI 84·1-87·9).

screen.reason: The study includes a multireader multicase (MRMC) trial evaluating the diagnostic impact and efficiency of AI assistance compared to unassisted clinician review across 28 otolaryngologists.
